explanation: Searched Mathlib's `Data/Nat/Factorization/*` (Basic, Defs, PrimePow, Induction) and the whole Mathlib tree. All occurrences of `ordCompl` in Mathlib are collected (Basic.lean lemmas such as `ordCompl_pos`, `ordCompl_mul`, `not_dvd_ordCompl`, `ordCompl_self_pow`, `factorization_ordCompl`, plus uses in Bernoulli, DirichletCharacter, ZMod/UnitsCyclic, PrimePow), and none of them relates `ordCompl` to `Nat.gcd`; grep for `gcd` together with `ordCompl` returns no matches. The closest general statements are `Nat.factorization_gcd` (`(gcd a b).factorization = a.factorization ⊓ b.factorization`) and the coprime/gcd cancellation lemmas (`Nat.Coprime.gcd_mul_right_cancel_right` etc.), but deriving the splitting formula from these would need an argument of substance (nonzeroness of both sides, factorizations of products and powers, appeal to `Nat.eq_of_factorization_eq`), so it is not a one- or two-line specialization. A further grep for statements of the shape `gcd … p ^ … min` in `Data/Nat` found nothing. Hence no Mathlib declaration states or directly yields `Nat.gcd m n = Nat.gcd (ordCompl[p] m) (ordCompl[p] n) * p ^ min (m.factorization p) (n.factorization p)`; the library's proof indeed uses only Mathlib ingredients (`Nat.ordProj_mul_ordCompl_eq_self`, `Nat.not_dvd_ordCompl`) together with its own `gcd_pow_mul_pow_mul`.
